episodes.215237: A warm front slowly lifting across the Mid-Atlantic resulted in multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms. A few of the storms produced sporadic gale-force wind gusts around southern Maryland, just on the cool side of the front positioned off to the west.
episodes.215238: A warm front slowly lifting across the Mid-Atlantic resulted in multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms. The round of storms that came through during the late afternoon and early evening produced some sporadic, localized wind damage where storms clustered into bands.
episodes.215266: A weak cold front sparked scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours. A couple of these storms became severe with localized damaging wind gusts near Charlottesville and southern Maryland.
episodes.215268: A weak cold front sparked scattered thunderstorms during the afternoon and evening hours. These storms developed into a cluster that produced gale-force winds over the middle to lower tidal Potomac River and the middle Chesapeake Bay area.
episodes.215279: A severe thunderstorm formed over the Little Rockies of southwest Phillips County, then moved southeast through southern Phillips County and Garfield County, bringing severe wind damage and heavy rainfall to some locations.
episodes.215362: A cold front moved through Middle Tennessee during the afternoon of August 17, 2026, which helped to develop thunderstorms across eastern and southern portions of the area. These thunderstorms posed a damaging wind threat, and one thunderstorm in Lawrenceburg downed a tree onto a vehicle and house.
episodes.215448: Hurricane Lala formed in the central Pacific and approached the islands from southeast. The hurricane passed just south of the Big Island, then moved northwest and passed south of the rest of the Hawaiian islands. Lala brought catastrophic damage to the Big Island of Hawaii in the form of massive flooding and wind damage. Considerable widespread damage due to the winds and flooding was also felt over the rest of the islands.
episodes.215806: Scattered thunderstorm activity associated with weak shortwaves passing through the Tennessee Valley region resulted in several reports of wind damage over the span of two afternoons and evenings.
episodes.216244: Rounds of rain and thunderstorms continued into the middle of August as a front remained in the vicinity on the 15th, lifted north as a warm front on the 16th, and then a cold front passed through on the 17th. ||Some strong to severe thunderstorms were noted during this timeframe, with daily observations of downed trees and power lines in northeast Kentucky from the 15th to the 17th. 72-hour rainfall amounts generally ranged from one to three inches, although some pockets of three to five inches were observed. Seemingly endless rounds of precipitation during the first half of the month had already saturated soils across much of the area. Thus, even lesser rainfall amounts were needed to cause some roadway flooding in northeast Kentucky.
episodes.216245: Rounds of rain and thunderstorms continued into the middle of August as a front remained in the vicinity of southeast Ohio on the 15th, lifted north as a warm front on the 16th, and then a cold front passed through on the 17th. ||Daily showers and thunderstorms that pressed through the area during this time casted swaths of tree and power line damage across southeast Ohio. Additionally, 72-hour rainfall amounts generally ranged from one to three inches, although some pockets of three to five inches were also observed. Seemingly endless rounds of precipitation during the first half of the month had already saturated soils across much of the area. Thus, even lesser rainfall amounts resulted in flooded roads and rises on creeks and streams in southeast Ohio. Impacts from heavier rain also included water rescues, some flooded structures, and river flooding on Duck Creek, Sunday Creek.
episodes.216246: Rounds of rain and thunderstorms continued in West Virginia as a front remained in the vicinity on August 15th, lifted north as a warm front on the 16th, and then a cold front passed through on the 17th. 72-hour rainfall amounts generally ranged from one to three inches, though some pockets of three to five inches were observed. Seemingly endless rounds of precipitation during the first half of the month had already saturated soils across much of the area. Thus, even lesser rainfall amounts resulted in flooded roads across portions of West Virginia. Impacts from heavier rain also included water rescues, flooded structures, and river flooding on Clear Fork, Sand Run, Elk Twomile Creek, Tygart Valley River, West Fork River, and Middle Island Creek. Additionally, episodic rounds of strong thunderstorms produced during this timeframe resulted in more downed trees and power lines across the state. This occurred in locations that had already faced powerful storms earlier in the month, adding to the total of storm damage costs.
episodes.216312: Several strong to severe storms tracked across far southeastern Wyoming and into western Nebraska, all along the North Platte River Valley. A few storms produced large hail.
episodes.216360: Scattered thunderstorms moved across eastern Colorado. Heavy rain with isolated flash flooding occurred. Flooding appeared to be brief and limited to flowing over roadways. Isolated hail and strong winds reported as well from the thunderstorms.
episodes.216435: A southward moving cold front advanced through northern MN on the evening of August 17th. Increasing moisture at the surface sliding in from South Dakota converged on an unstable airmass that generated showers and thunderstorms along the boundary.  Additionally, sufficient wind shear aloft aided in the production of quarter size hail near the city of Bertha in Todd County.
episodes.216471: An isolated storm dove southeast out of South Dakota and dropped severe hail just inside the CWA border. The storm weaked and briefly re-strengthened before disapating near Alliance. Severe Thunderstorm Watch 592.
episodes.216526: A cluster of storms across West Virginia and Virginia spawned isolated to scattered afternoon and evening thunderstorms across central North Carolina. The strongest cells produced damaging wind reports across Person, Granville, Orange, Alamance, Guilford, and Davidson Counties.
episodes.216557: A cluster of strong thunderstorms moved into northeastern Oklahoma from the west-northwest during the morning of the 17th. These thunderstorms intensified as they moved east-southeast, and produced widespread damaging wind gusts across the area.
episodes.216558: A cluster of severe thunderstorms moved across northeastern Oklahoma and through northwestern Arkansas during the morning of the 17th. These thunderstorms produced widespread damaging wind gusts across the area.
episodes.216573: Multiple rounds of showers and thunderstorms produced a few wind gusts in excess of 34 knots.
episodes.216577: Isolated to scattered storms developed ahead of a cold front across the northwest and northern Piedmont of central North Carolina during the late afternoon and evening hours. A few storms producing damaging winds across Orange, Alamance, and Forsyth Counties.
episodes.216848: Clusters of storms tracked from north central to central South Dakota on the afternoon and evening of August 17th into the early morning of August 18th. A peak wind gust of 63 mph was recorded at the South Dakota Department of Transportation mesonet station 3 miles north of Gann Valley, with a 62 mph gust recorded on the Huron Remote Automated Weather Station (RAWS) in southeast Hand county. Higher winds, likely on the order of 70 to 80 mph, caused damage in northern Stanley county, with the roof blown off a shop and 15 power poles broken along South Dakota Highway 63.
episodes.217011: Typical summer weather prevailed with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.
episodes.217465: In the wake of overnight thunderstorm activity, instability built up during the late morning and early afternoon hours of August 16th, with 1500-2000 J/kg of surface-based CAPE developing. Storm activity renewed by midday in western Ohio, associated with a mesoscale convective vortex. Sufficient deep shear allowed separate storm clusters to consolidate into a larger line that swept across eastern Ohio during the early to mid afternoon hours. The result was widespread reports of wind damage, mainly to trees. One person in Muskingum County was injured by a falling tree. A few isolated instances of flash flooding also occurred due to the multiple storm rounds.
episodes.217593: Thunderstorms during the afternoon hours produced locally heavy rainfall.
episodes.217602: During the late afternoon and early evening of Monday, August 17, 2026, an advancing cold front sparked isolated severe thunderstorms across north-central and northeastern Minnesota. Other than some isolated tree damage and sub-severe hail, storms remained below severe limits.
episodes.217639: Numerous multi-cell thunderstorms developed near a quasi-stationary boundary across central Oklahoma on the afternoon and evening of the 16th. Several areas of thunderstorm wind damage were observed due to downbursts, including on the northeast sides of Norman, OK.
episodes.217709: On August 13th, strong heating under ridging created enough surface based instability to pulse up storms inland that moved southeasterly into inland southeast Georgia in the afternoon. Slightly drier air increased the chance of downbursts (DCAPE 1000 J/kg) especially along boundary collisions. On August 14th, ���heat wave��� ridging over the southeastern U.S. combined with a deeply moist and unstable airmass triggered pulse thunderstorms and sea breeze thunderstorms to develop in the afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.217828: A cluster of storms tracked along a boundary from central Arkansas into north Mississippi during the afternoon hours of August 17th. A very unstable airmass north of the boundary provided the fuel for severe storms that produced damaging winds from east-central Arkansas to northeast Mississippi.
episodes.217829: A cluster of storms tracked along a boundary from central Arkansas into north Mississippi during the afternoon hours of August 17th. A very unstable airmass north of the boundary provided the fuel for severe storms that produced damaging winds from east-central Arkansas to northeast Mississippi.
episodes.217936: Severe thunderstorms including several supercells developed across west central MN during the late afternoon hours. These storms produced large hail and severe wind gusts. The maximum reported hail size for this episode was tennis ball size near New York Mills, MN.
episodes.218011: A cold front and supportive midlevel low helped set the stage for numerous thunderstorms to develop across the region. Heavy rainfall rates resulted, leading to both flash flooding and severe thunderstorm wind damage in southwestern Virginia.
episodes.218012: A cold front and supportive midlevel low helped set the stage for numerous thunderstorms to develop across the region. Heavy rainfall rates resulted, leading to both flash flooding and severe thunderstorm wind damage East Tennessee. These thunderstorms eventually congealed into a line or mesoscale convective system and moved to the southwest towards North Carolina.
episodes.218104: Training showers and thunderstorms create isolated flooding in Wetzel County.
episodes.218160: Scattered to widespread thunderstorms formed across the central to western combined OK/TX Panhandles, eventually spreading north. With these storms there were a few isolated severe wind gusts in Hartley and Carson counties in the Texas Panhandle. The gusts measured in Hartley County topped out at 64 mph while one gust in Carson County was measured at 69 mph.
episodes.218239: During the late afternoon and evening hours of August 15th, isolated showers and thunderstorms developed and progressed over north central Kentucky near the Bluegrass region. With afternoon high temperatures in the 90s and dew points in the low-to-mid 70s, this helped produce MLCAPE values up to around 2500-3000 J/kg. While weaker wind shear did limit the extent of convective development, the higher instability and ample moisture in the form of PW greater than 2 did result in isolated thunderstorm wind damage and flash flooding. During the late afternoon through the late evening hours of the 16th, scattered thunderstorms moved over southern Indiana and north central Kentucky ahead of a cold front passing through the Ohio Valley. While there was meager deep-layer shear in place, a 30-40 kt LLJ, ample instability of MLCAPE around 2500-3000 J/kg, and decent moisture with PW over 1.8 helped result in some thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts and damage.
episodes.218241: During the late afternoon through the late evening hours of the 16th, scattered thunderstorms moved over southern Indiana and north central Kentucky ahead of a cold front passing through the Ohio Valley. While there was meager deep-layer shear in place, a 30-40 kt LLJ, ample instability of MLCAPE around 2500-3000 J/kg, and decent moisture with PW over 1.8 helped result in some thunderstorms producing severe wind gusts and damage.
episodes.218258: At about 9pm on August 16th, a broken line of thunderstorms entered St. Louis County. The primary cell caused structural damage in Chesterfield before morphing into a more linear structure and causing tree damage in University City.
episodes.218264: Slow moving thunderstorms brough minor instances of severe weather and a report of flooding.
episodes.218266: The Black Hills saw two days of marginal severe weather, that brought wind and hail to the Black Hills and surrounding areas.
episodes.218278: A warm and unstable airmass was in place ahead of a convectively augmented vortex, leading to evening scattered strong storm development across the region with gusty winds.
episodes.218279: A warm and unstable airmass was in place ahead of a convectively augmented vortex, leading to evening scattered strong storm development across the region with heavy rain and flooding.
episodes.218413: A weakening mesoscale convective system moved from generally north to south out of Kentucky into southwestern Virginia. This complex brought severe thunderstorm winds to portions of southwestern Virginia.
episodes.218414: A strong line of thunderstorms known as a mesoscale convective system brought damaging thunderstorm winds to southwest North Carolina.
episodes.218492: A broken line of strong to severe thunderstorms moved into western North Carolina from east Tennessee in advance of a cold front during the evening. Multiple embedded severe storms produced areas of damaging wind gusts across the mountains and foothills.

Sunday Creek at Glouster exceeded a bankfull level of 13 feet on the evening of August 17th. The creek continued to rise to a crest near 13.6 feet that night, then receded below bankfull again shortly after midnight. While the creek was out of its banks, impacts included flooding of Oakdale Road, South Town Street, Kennedy Road, and Glouster Memorial Park.
